title: Jehoshaphat, King of Judah
lead: Jehoshaphat, "the LORD judges," ruled Judah about 870–848 BC. He made peace with Ahab's house and fought beside Ahab and his son, and Chronicles remembers him as a teacher of the law, a reformer of the courts and the king whose army won by singing.

sections.b: Kings tells of his alliance with Ahab at Ramoth-gilead, where Micaiah prophesied (1 Kings 22), his campaign with Jehoram of Israel against Moab, where Elisha prophesied (2 Kings 3), and his failed ships at Ezion-geber (1 Kings 22:48–49). Chronicles adds his teachers of the law (2 Chronicles 17:7–9), his judges (19:4–11), the prayer and victory in the Valley of Beracah (20:1–30) and prophetic rebukes for his alliances (19:2–3; 20:37). Joel's "Valley of Jehoshaphat," where God judges the nations, plays on the meaning of the name (Joel 3:2, 12).
